name: Web Audio API
runtime_requirements: browser with Web Audio API support
notes: Spec 17: this is a browser capability, not an install. Ship a capability check and a fallback, not an install step. Detection: `typeof (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext) === 'function'`. Fallback: HTMLAudioElement playback for straight playback, and disable synthesis/analysis features when absent. An AudioContext starts suspended until a user gesture resumes it, so treat that resume as part of the capability path. A browser platform API has no distributable artefact and therefore no package licence; license_class is LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED only because the enum has no not-applicable value. No licence review is actually needed to call the API.

A browser platform API has no distributable artefact and therefore no package licence; license_class is LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED only because the enum has no not-applicable value. name: WebCodecs
notes: Spec 17: this is a browser capability, not an install. Ship a capability check and a fallback, not an install step. Detection is two-stage and both stages matter: `typeof VideoDecoder !== 'undefined'` for the API, then `await VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported(config)` for the specific codec, because the object existing says nothing about H.264 or AV1 being available. Fallback: a WebAssembly decoder, or Media Source Extensions (id 305) for plain playback. Browser coverage is uneven across engines and platforms, so treat the per-codec probe as required, not optional. A browser platform API has no distributable artefact and therefore no package licence; license_class is LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED only because the enum has no not-applicable value. No licence review is actually needed to call the API.

name: Media Source Extensions
runtime_requirements: browser with Media Source Extensions support
notes: Spec 17: this is a browser capability, not an install. Ship a capability check and a fallback, not an install step. Detection: `'MediaSource' in window` plus `MediaSource.isTypeSupported(mime)` for the codec, and `'ManagedMediaSource' in window` for iOS Safari, which withheld plain MediaSource on iPhone for years. Fallback: native HLS via a plain `<video src>` on Safari, or progressive download. This is the substrate hls.js (id 308) and dash.js (id 309) are built on, which is why both report unsupported outside a browser. A browser platform API has no distributable artefact and therefore no package licence; license_class is LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED only because the enum has no not-applicable value. No licence review is actually needed to call the API.

name: MediaRecorder API
runtime_requirements: user permission for getUserMedia when recording capture devices
notes: Spec 17: this is a browser capability, not an install. Ship a capability check and a fallback, not an install step. Detection: `typeof MediaRecorder !== 'undefined'` then `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported(mime)`, because the supported container/codec set differs sharply between engines (WebM/Opus versus MP4/AAC). Fallback: capture raw frames through an AudioWorklet (id 297) or canvas and encode client-side or server-side. Requires a secure context, and a user permission prompt whenever the stream comes from a microphone or camera. A browser platform API has no distributable artefact and therefore no package licence; license_class is LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED only because the enum has no not-applicable value. No licence review is actually needed to call the API.

name: FAISS
notes: Measured in a dedicated venv at technology-universe/runtimes/python-ai (Python 3.12.14, macOS arm64). Licence MIT, read from the installed distribution metadata. name: Annoy
notes: Measured in a dedicated venv at technology-universe/runtimes/python-ai (Python 3.12.14, macOS arm64). Licence Apache-2.0, read from the installed distribution metadata. Built from source during install (a cp312 arm64 wheel was produced locally). Smoke test: built a 4-tree euclidean index over 10 vectors and ran `get_nns_by_item`. Annoy indexes are immutable once built and are memory-mapped from disk, which is the trade it makes against hnswlib's incremental inserts.

name: Chroma
notes: Measured in a dedicated venv at technology-universe/runtimes/python-ai (Python 3.12.14, macOS arm64). Licence Apache-2.0, read from the installed distribution metadata. Embeddings were supplied explicitly on purpose — Chroma's default embedding function would download an ONNX model on first use, and no model artefacts were fetched during this work. name: Qdrant
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no port was bound and no data directory created, so no version was measured. Operational note for whoever deploys it: the default configuration exposes the REST and gRPC APIs without an API key, so an API key or network policy must be set before the container is reachable from anything but localhost. name: Milvus
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official container image `milvusdb/milvus`, normally via the project's compose file or Helm chart. Licence Apache-2.0. The important deployment fact is that Milvus is not a single process: even the standalone mode expects etcd for metadata and an S3-compatible object store for segments, and the distributed mode adds several more components, so the compose or Kubernetes path is the realistic one and resource requirements are substantially higher than the other engines in this category. Set credentials explicitly; do not ship the sample stack's default MinIO keys.

name: Weaviate Community
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official container image `semitechnologies/weaviate`, via compose or the official Helm chart. name: LanceDB
notes: Measured in a dedicated venv at technology-universe/runtimes/python-ai (Python 3.12.14, macOS arm64). Licence Apache-2.0, read from the installed distribution metadata. Smoke test: connected to a temporary directory, created a table from two eight-dimensional vectors and returned one search hit. Embedded and file-based rather than a server: the store is a directory of Lance-format files, which is why it also works against object storage and in serverless shapes where a long-running database process is not available. The Rust core is also published as a crate and as an npm package for Node.

name: pgvector
runtime_requirements: C toolchain and PostgreSQL development headers when building
notes: Not standalone: pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension, so it has no version or lifecycle of its own and depends entirely on PostgreSQL, inventory id 386. It is installed into an existing server and then enabled per database with `CREATE EXTENSION vector`, which means an install without a running PostgreSQL of a matching major version is meaningless. Not installed here; no PostgreSQL server was provisioned for this work, so no version was measured. Acquisition options are the Homebrew formula `pgvector`, distribution packages such as postgresql-16-pgvector, a source build against pg_config, or the prebuilt `pgvector/pgvector` container image which bundles both. Licence is the PostgreSQL License, a permissive licence in the BSD family. Note also that the PyPI package named `pgvector` is only a client-side type adapter, not the extension itself.

name: Vespa
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official container image `vespaengine/vespa`. Licence Apache-2.0. Vespa is the heaviest engine in this category by a wide margin: it is a distributed serving platform with its own application-package deployment model and configuration server, so it needs several GB of RAM even for a single-node trial and cannot be treated as a drop-in vector store. Budget for the operational model, not just the image pull.

name: OpenSearch
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official container image `opensearchproject/opensearch`; a Homebrew formula also exists and its local metadata confirms the Apache-2.0 licence (formula `opensearch`, stable 3.8.0), which is the evidence used here rather than an assumption. This is the fork of Elasticsearch 7.10 that stayed Apache-2.0 after Elastic's relicensing, and that licence difference is the main reason to choose it over id 356. Operational note: recent versions require a strong admin password to be supplied at first start and will refuse to boot with the old default credentials — set it explicitly and never carry a sample password into a deployment.

name: Elasticsearch
license: Elastic License 2.0 / SSPL-1.0 (dual; AGPL-3.0 offered as a third option in recent 8.x releases)
notes: Licensing is the load-bearing fact on this record, and it is not plain open source. Since 7.11 Elasticsearch has been distributed under a dual Elastic License 2.0 / SSPL-1.0 scheme; neither is an OSI-approved open-source licence, and the SSPL in particular imposes source obligations on anyone offering the software as a service. Recent 8.x releases add AGPL-3.0 as a third option, so which terms apply depends on the exact version — verify per release rather than assuming. license_class is SOURCE_AVAILABLE for that reason, and production_status is review-required: redistribution or managed-service use needs legal sign-off before deployment. OpenSearch (id 355) is the Apache-2.0 fork if those terms are unacceptable. Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official image from docker.elastic.co. Set the elastic user's password explicitly at first boot.

name: Meilisearch
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official container image `getmeili/meilisearch`; a Homebrew formula also exists and its local metadata confirms the MIT licence (formula `meilisearch`, stable 1.53.1), which is the evidence used here rather than an assumption. Single binary with no JVM and no external dependencies, which makes it by far the lightest engine in this category. Operational note: a master key must be supplied for production mode, and without one the instance runs unauthenticated — set MEILI_MASTER_KEY explicitly and never reuse a sample value.

name: Typesense
notes: Service, deliberately not run during this work; no version measured. Acquisition is the official container image `typesense/typesense`. Licence note that matters for anyone embedding rather than deploying: the Typesense server is GPL-3.0-or-later, unlike the MIT/Apache-2.0 engines elsewhere in this category, while the client libraries are permissively licensed. Running it as a separate service over HTTP is the normal shape and does not create obligations for the calling application, but linking or bundling the server does. Operational note: an API key must be supplied at start-up via --api-key; choose a real secret rather than a sample value.
